title: Schema versioning and graceful fallbacks for legacy tool calls
creator: Aesha Patel
description: Background: As we onboard more third-party and customer-defined tool schemas, we see two pain points: (1) runtime failures when callers use legacy or slightly different parameter shapes, and (2) poor observability into why a tool call was rejected. This ticket defines a versioned JSON schema format and the runtime fallback behavior to permit safe, auditable compatibility with older clients while preserving a path to strict validation for new deployments. The design emphasizes clear error codes, deterministic coercions, and an opt-in 'lenient' validation mode for routes that require backwards compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a schema header field ($schema_version) and validator rules that allow runtime to select strict or lenient validation per route
Provide at least three deterministic coercions (string->int, int->string, single-value array unwrap) with audit log entries for each applied coercion
Define a small error taxonomy (E_SCHEMA_MISSING, E_TYPE_MISMATCH, E_UNKNOWN_FIELD, E_COERCION_FAILED) and surface machine-readable error_code + human_message in API responses
Implement server-side fallback routing for deprecated parameter names via a routing map configurable in the model/tool manifest
End-to-end tests that simulate legacy clients and assert no behavioral regressions for strict routes
Document the schema header and compatibility modes in the developer docs and include migration guidance for customers
tasks: Spec: draft JSON schema header format and validation modes (Aesha)
Runtime: integrate version selector into parameter parsing pipeline (Jamal)
Runtime: implement deterministic coercion library with unit tests
Console: add UI flag for enabling lenient validation on a tool endpoint (Design + Frontend)
Telemetry: emit validation events with error_code and coercion_applied boolean
Doc: write migration guide and examples for common legacy shapes (confluence link below)
QA: create fuzz tests exercising unknown fields and arrays-vs-scalar cases
comments: 2025-02-14 Aesha: Kickoff doc created and shared in #infra-apis. Initial spec now lives in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/TOOLS/Schema+Compatibility+Strategy

2025-02-17 Jamal: Spiked on integrating a schema header. Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124. Prototype shows hooking into parse stage and returning structured error objects.
2025-02-19 Reviewer (Maya Gomez): Prefer explicit coercions only — avoid silent casting for floats to ints. Suggested adding a warning mode that logs but still rejects when strict=true.
2025-02-21 Aesha: Updated spec to include error taxonomy and telemetry fields. Added example mapping for deprecated params: { 'userId' -> 'user_id' } stored in tool manifest.

2025-02-24 Jamal: Implemented coercion library; currently supports string->int, string->bool, single-item array unwrap. Tests added in runtime:tests/validation_coercions_test.go. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3167
2025-02-26 QA (Liu Wei): Found edge case where nested unknown fields inside objects are flattened by our prior mapper. Added task to change behavior to reject unknown nested keys unless lenient=true.
notes: Design trade-offs: lenient=true reduces customer friction but increases ambiguity in intent. We make lenient opt-in per-route and require audit logs for every coercion to curb silent breakages.
Performance: validation added ~0.6ms median to parse path in prototype. We'll benchmark at scale; consider sampling telemetry for high-throughput endpoints.

Rollout plan: feature gate behind runtime-1.26, enable for internal tooling first, then offer as toggle in Console for customers. Deprecation window for legacy param names: 90 days once telemetry shows <1% usage
